entries.title: Jeremiah 3:1
segments:
Played the harlot; by idolatry, which is spiritual fornication.  So it is represented throughout the book. 
 
  Yet return; God in his great mercy is ever ready to recieve the true penitent.

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:2
segments:
Sat for them; waited for thy lovers. 
 
  As the Arabian; as he lies in wait to rob travellers.

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:5
segments: Will he reserve his anger for ever? will not God pardon thine iniquity as soon as thou comest to him in true penitence?

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:8
segments: Put her away--given her a bill; by giving her over to captivity.

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:11
segments: Backsliding Israel--treacherous Judah; Judah is more guilty than Israel, because she has failed to take warning from God's judgments upon her sister nation.
When men refuse to take warning from the punishment of those whose sinful example they are imitating, they aggravate their guilt, and bring upon themselves severer judgments.

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:12
segments:
Toward the north; where Israel was held in captivity. 
 
vv 12.15. 
 
God waits to be acknowledged in the calamities which he sends upon his people; and when they return to him by hearty confession and repentance, he will graciously accept them, and restore them to more than their former prosperity.

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:14
segments: One of a city--two of a family; that is, a remnant of you shall be saved.  This purpose of God respecting both Judah and Israel is often repeated in the Old Testament.

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:16
segments: The ark--of the Lord; the former glory of the ark shall be forgotten in comparison with the greater glory of the future.  Compare

.  At the same time the prophet intimates the removal of this outward symbol of God's presence, which took place at the captivity. 
 
The glory of the gospel dispensation is such that, in comparison, there is no glory in the old dispensation which preceded it, and prepared the way for it.

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:17
segments: All the nations shall be gathered; a prophecy which can have its complete fulfilment only in "the last days" of the Christian dispensation.  See

. 
 
Though in the establishment of his church God began with one nation, it was from the beginning his plan to extend it from that nation over all the earth.  The calling of the Gentiles is the fulfilment of the original promise, "In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed."

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:18
segments: With the house of Israel; in harmony with it.

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:19
segments: When we cleave to God, as children to a father, with a free and willing spirit, he fulfils to us his promises; and when he sends forth the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, we cry, "Abba, Father;" to us belongs the childlike obedience, and to him the glory of it.

entries.title: Jeremiah 3:21
segments:
vv 21-25. 
 
  A voice was heard; in these words the prophet anticipates the repentance and supplication of Israel.
